q: Why is potty training so freaking HARD!? I’ve been trying since February. Some days we make great progress but then soon after we regress.
cx: Mother of a 2y7m-old, three months into training.

q: I am so tired I want to scream and yell and cry. We’ve had 6 accidents today and it’s barely 5pm. I’m ready to quit.
We both just had a huge meltdown and I feel like a horrible mother. I don’t know if I should just quit or keep pushing thru.
cx: Two of six accidents happened on the way to the potty.

q: At first staying commando was working so I just let her be naked but now she’s having accidents while being naked so idek 😭
I hate how all the “I potty trained my toddler in 3 days” videos made me think it would be easy.
EVERYTHING IS A FIGHT. EVERYTHING. For almost 6 months now, bedtime and nap time ends with us putting a screaming toddler into a crib and him screaming his head off for the first hour.
cx: Parent of a three-year-old and a three-month-old.

q: I’m actually a licensed therapist too so I feel well versed in co regulation with a toddler and using language that validates his feelings all while sticking to the boundary and expectations at hand.   Why isn’t he getting any better? Science says he should be getting better.
cx: Consistent follow-through for months with no change.

q: I believed that as long as I am consistent and I don’t cave, and I ride out the tantrum, then they will decrease over time. BUT THEY DON’T.
I’m terrified to potty train or transition to a bed because he’s so defiant, control hungry, and puts up a fight to everything.
cx: New baby and new daycare in the last few months.

q: I just need someone to say, “I’ve been there. Nothing seems to work and that’s ok. Your kid is normal. He will figure it out as he gets older”.
he’s an angel for other people. His teachers constantly praise us for how well behaved he is at daycare. […] But the moment he is home and with us, he unleashes.
I said to my husband that this phase requires high effort but very little reward :/
I stay home with her all day and it has gotten to the point I am unable to do anything. I can’t clean the house or do anything for myself until she falls asleep.
cx: Mother of a 17-month-old who cries whether she is beside her or not.

q: My partner doesn’t understand because he only gets to see us for a few hours in the evening. She rarely cries around him.
I should be strong enough to handle my own baby crying but these past few days it has enraged me.
He’s b\*\*tching that it stinks, it’s unsanitary and she needs to learn to use the big toilet because his nieces never used a small potty. He threw it out!
cx: Four weekends into training a nearly three-year-old; the father removed the small potty.

q: Today she gets home from daycare full refusal, won’t sit, full blown meltdown, is holding it to the point she’s crying, I gave up put a pull up on and put her to sleep.
cx: Two days after the potty was thrown out.

q: She wears pull ups at school, while she will sit on the school toilet, she will not release.

Potty watch: this one is iffy. She will follow the potty watch, if she chooses to. Based on her progress, I set it to every 90 minutes. If she doesn’t feel like it, she’ll press the button to silence it.
cx: List of what was tried, after charts and bribes.

q: Potty charts and stickers: she has no interest, doesn’t care about them, is more likely to rip it down then follow it. The magnetic one has just become a new toy.

My goal was to get her potty trained by her birthday in late July, or at least by September. I want to move her to a daycare closer to home, but they all require kids older than 2.5 be fully potty trained.
I’d be hard pressed to complement him. All parenting is done by me.
cx: Told to praise the father's effort.

q: Seeing parents with multiple kids close in age has made me realize parenting is survival mode sometimes regardless of whether you have boys or girls lol.
cx: After in-laws' one-year-old emptied the cabinets on Mother's Day.

q: I keep my cool with her, I get down on her level I try to have her express emotions and all I get back is her screaming “no” or “don’t talk to me like that”
Tonight she told me it makes her sad when I yell at her like that, and I had not yelled at her at all, all day! I don’t even know what to do im at a loss.
cx: Child uses feelings language against the parent.

q: I will say I notice her coming home everyday with some new bad influence from her friends so I wonder if this too is something like that?
if we try to leave her she grabs us and screams at us to stay with her so it sometimes adds fuel to the fire, but I agree we always try to tell her she needs a minute alone and to take deep breaths
cx: Response to advice to give space.

q: She doesnt care about rewards of any kind, she doesn't care about privileges being taken away, she doesn't care about how the mess feels in her pull up or in underwear.
cx: Three-year-old who has shown she can use the toilet.

q: I just want to pull my hair out. Please any advice or kind words.

The most frustrating thing though is that its only really at home or when she is with me (mom) she very rarely has accidents at nursery, she doesn't have accidents when she is with my family members while im at work but if im around she will.
cx: Trained in five days last June; accidents crept back.

q: Ive tried the timer method, ive tried putting it all in her hands so she is in full control. We have a potty that she isnt interested in anymore.
I truly feel disheartened and feel like im doing something wrong.
Im more frustrated about the fact its only with me that it happens but anywhere else or with anyone else she is perfect 🤦🏻‍♀️
I’ve tried it all. Giving him options, letting him pick, giving him a heads up, natural consequences (no playground or going outside without putting clothes on).
I feel like an idiot that she’s over 2 & isn’t potty trained.
cx: Mother recovering from surgery, unable to lift her daughter.

q: I can’t go anywhere. For one, he melts down anytime we try to go into a store. I got kicked out of the eye doctor the other day because he wouldn’t stop screaming.
People literally cover their ears, gasp, and practically run away. People can’t handle how insanely loud it is.
I have tried EVERYTHING, but nothing stops him. I’m losing my mind. My nerves can’t handle this. I have never met a child like this before.
I got frustrated this afternoon because I put him on the potty three separate times and each time he’d have an accident after he got off the potty. Am I just starting it too early?
I’m 28 weeks pregnant and really wanted him to be able to use the potty so I don’t have two kids in diapers but I seem to need to lower my expectations.

Yesterday we went to Walmart and I wouldn’t let her run around doing whatever she wanted, so when I picked her up to put her back in the cart she was acting awful I just about left the cart there and went home without anything she was screaming so loud.
I can’t even cook without her screaming at me to be in the living room with her. Not playing with her just there existing while she does whatever 🫩

I just finished reading the Oh Crap method and I’m planning to try to follow it with some adjustments as needed.   But! We’re expecting her baby brother end of June/beginning of July, AND we are moving in the beginning of June.
I also think it would be hard to potty train a toddler with a newborn…
I don’t want to hear “just let her wear leggings” because it’s not what I want.
cx: Three-year-old in hot Texas refuses shorts.

q: But basically it comes down a respect/ listening thing.  If she cannot listen to me and respect my wishes as a parent, then she gets less choice.
cx: Why she removes the long sleeves and leggings.
